brand.story: Wessuwan is named after Thao Wessuwan, the guardian king in Thai and Buddhist tradition who protects people from evil and guards their treasure. Today the evil comes by phone, and Wessuwan protects people and their savings.

home.title: Stop phone scams before the money moves
home.lead: Wessuwan listens to calls from unknown numbers and, the moment a caller uses scam tactics, warns the person on the phone and texts their family, before any money moves.
home.problem: Scammers pretend to be the tax office, the bank, the police or a grandchild in trouble. They create fear and urgency, then ask for gift cards, crypto, a "safe account" transfer or a verification code. Older adults lose the most, often alone on the phone with no one to ask.
home.how1: Calls from unknown numbers hear a short notice, then speech-to-text transcribes both sides live.
home.how2: After each caller sentence, an AI checks for scam tactics: urgency, threats, posing as the bank or police, requests for codes, money or secrecy.
home.how3: At high risk, a calm voice warning plays in the call and the family gets an SMS with a one-tap way to call.
home.privacy: We can't leak what we don't keep. Audio is never stored. Normal calls are deleted the moment they end. Trusted contacts are never processed. Only a short encrypted summary of a detected scam is kept, for 30 days.

setup.title: Setup
setup.intro: Set up protection for one person. Everything here can be changed or deleted at any time.
setup.demoNotice: This is the public demo: you are looking at sample settings and nothing can be changed.
setup.statusOff: Protection is OFF: calls ring straight through and nothing is processed
setup.statusNoConsent: Protection is not active yet: record consent below
setup.name: Name (used in family alerts, e.g. "Mom")
setup.number: Their phone number (calls are forwarded to it)
setup.consentText: Wessuwan listens to calls from numbers that are not on your trusted list, to warn you about scams. Before any call is checked, the caller hears: "This call is protected by Wessuwan, an AI scam protection service." The conversation is turned into text by a speech-to-text service and checked by an AI service while the call is happening. Audio is never saved. Normal calls are deleted as soon as they end. If a scam is detected, your family gets a text message and a short summary is kept, encrypted, for {days} days. You can turn protection off or delete all your data at any time.
setup.consentAgree: I am the protected person (or their legal representative) and I agree.
setup.consentAllParty: In {country} all parties must know about the listening. The announcement is mandatory and always on.
setup.consentOneParty: The announcement plays on every call, in every country.
setup.trustedHint: One number per line. Family and friends ring straight through.
setup.familyHint: One number per line. They get an SMS when a scam is detected.
setup.testMock: Demo mode: this message was NOT sent. Preview: {text}
setup.forward1: Wessuwan answers calls first, then rings the protected person's real phone. Your Wessuwan (Twilio) number is {twilio}.
setup.forward2: Recommended: make the Wessuwan number the one people call. Give it to banks, doctors and new contacts, and update it wherever the old number is listed. Keep the real number for trusted family.
setup.forward3: Alternative: on the protected person's phone, forward only unanswered calls to the Wessuwan number (most carriers: dial **61*{twilio}#). Do not forward all calls unconditionally: Wessuwan rings the real number, so the call would loop.
setup.forward4: Then call the Wessuwan number from a phone that is not a trusted contact to test it.
setup.dangerText: Deletes all scam summaries, trusted contacts, family numbers and the consent record, and turns protection off. This cannot be undone.
setup.deleted: All data deleted. Protection is off.
setup.summariesKept: Encrypted scam summaries kept: {n} (deleted automatically after {days} days)
